Maximiliano Hernández Martínez: President of El Salvador from 1931 to 1934 and 1935 to 1944.

Serving as the Soviet Union's largely ceremonial head of state from 1919 to 1946 while real power sat with Stalin, this former metalworker had been mayor of Petrograd after the October Revolution — who was he?
Grand Duke Michael Alexandrovich of Russia
Often depicted as King Arthur's sister, this ambiguous enchantress from medieval legend could be portrayed as either a healing fairy or a dangerous sorceress — who is she?

Morgan le Fay: Enchantress in the Arthurian legend. A significant aspect in many of Morgan's medieval and later iterations is the unpredictable duality of her nature, with potential for both good and evil.

Chief minister of his state for 13 years, this politician rose to become India's prime minister in 2014 and is now India's longest-serving PM outside the Indian National Congress. He was introduced to a paramilitary organization at age eight. Who is he?
Narendra Modi: Prime Minister of India since 2014. Narendra Damodardas Modi (born 17 September 1950) is an Indian politician who has served as the prime minister of India since 26 May 2014.
Nicknamed the 'Expressway Man of India' for spearheading projects like the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, this politician has served as Minister of Road Transport since 2014 — who is he?
Sparked by a disputed 2004 presidential runoff marred by fraud allegations, these Kyiv-centered protests forced political change in Ukraine that winter — what are they called?

Orange Revolution: 2004–2005 political protests in Ukraine. The nationwide protests succeeded when the results of the original runoff were annulled, and a re-vote was ordered by Ukraine's Supreme Court for 26 December 2004.
Rising from aide-de-camp to Tsar Nicholas II to lieutenant general in World War I, this nobleman seized power in a 1918 coup to become hetman of a short-lived Ukrainian state — who is he?
Pavlo Skoropadsky: Ukrainian and Russian Cossack military and political official; Hetman of Ukraine (1918)
This Odawa war chief led Native Americans against the British in the Great Lakes region from 1763 to 1766, in a conflict that came to bear his name — who was he?
Pontiac (Odawa leader): 18th-century Native American war chief.

Conceived by Josh Wardle and launched on April Fools' Day 2017, this Reddit social experiment let users edit a single pixel on a shared canvas every several minutes — what was this collaborative project called?
R/place: Online social experiment on Reddit. r/place was a recurring collaborative project and social experiment hosted on the content aggregator site Reddit.
In 1682 this French explorer canoed the lower Mississippi to the Gulf and claimed its whole basin for France, naming it La Louisiane after Louis XIV. Who was he?
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
Jean-François de Galaup, comte de Lapérouse
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle: French explorer of North America (1643–1687)
René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle

This December 1989 uprising began in the city of Timișoara and ended with the swift trial and execution of a longtime Communist dictator and his wife — which nation's uprising, the only one of 1989 to end that way?
Romanian revolution: 1989 popular uprising in Romania.
Nicknamed "Sam Bahadur" — the Brave — and a Military Cross winner in WWII, he led India's army during the 1971 war with Pakistan and became the country's first field marshal. Which general was he?
Co-leading a pro-Kurdish party to double-digit vote shares in Turkey's 2015 elections, this politician ran for president from behind bars in 2018 after his 2016 imprisonment — who is he?
Selahattin Demirtaş: Turkish politician. Selahattin Demirtaş (born 10 April 1973) is a Kurdish politician, lawyer and author.
Imprisoned and tortured as a young dissident under the Ottomans and once sentenced to death by the French, he went on to become the first president of independent Syria in 1943 — who was he?
This is the act of occupying an empty building or plot you don't own, rent, or have permission to use — often the seed of shanty towns in developing cities — what's it called?
Representing the Goshamahal constituency in Hyderabad, this Indian politician served as a state assembly whip for the BJP in Telangana until 2025 — who is he?
T. Raja Singh: Indian politician. Thakur Raja Singh (born 15 April 1977) is an Indian politician from the state of Telangana.

Fought entirely on Carthaginian soil after King Masinissa's repeated raids provoked a doomed counterattack under Hasdrubal, which 149-146 BC conflict was the last and final clash between Rome and Carthage?
Third Punic War: War between Rome and Carthage (149–146 BC). The war was fought entirely within Carthaginian territory, in what is now northern Tunisia.
This branch of Marxism-Leninism is named for the Russian revolutionary who developed it alongside the Left Opposition and the Fourth International — what's it called?
Trotskyism: Variety of Marxism developed by Leon Trotsky.
Elected in 2000, this businessman-turned-politician became the first Mexican president since 1929 who wasn't from the long-dominant PRI party. Who broke that streak?
Vicente Fox: President of Mexico from 2000 to 2006.

Fought alongside a wider Georgian civil conflict, this early-1990s fight pitted government forces against separatists backed by North Caucasian militants, Cossacks, and the Russian military — which conflict?
War in Abkhazia (1992–1993): Conflict between Georgia and Abkhaz separatists.
After an evangelical conversion in 1785, this Yorkshire MP spent two decades leading the parliamentary fight that ended Britain's slave trade — who was he?
William Wilberforce: English politician and abolitionist (1759–1833)
What is this — “Aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti, consort of Shiva”?

Yoni: Aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti, consort of Shiva. Yoni (Sanskrit: योनि, IAST: yoni), sometimes called pindika, is an abstract or aniconic representation of the Hindu goddess Shakti.
Who among these was born first?
Joseph Schumpeter (born 1883) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?

Ivan Pavlov (born 1849) is the earliest of the four. Pavlov also conducted significant research on the physiology of digestion, for which he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1904.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is an astronomer?
Bruno Rossi is an astronomer. Bruno Benedetto Rossi ( ROSS-ee, Italian: [ˈbruːno beneˈdetto ˈrossi]; 13 April 1905 – 21 November 1993) was an Italian-American experimental physicist.
Which of these four is a mathematician?
Hilary Putnam is a mathematician. Outside philosophy, Putnam contributed to mathematics and computer science.
What is the atomic number of Indium?
Indium: It is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements.
What is the atomic number of Scandium?
Scandium is a chemical element; it has symbol Sc and atomic number 21.
In what year was Stephen Hawking born?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Richard Sackler born?
Richard Sackler: Sackler and Purdue's role in the epidemic led to many lawsuits and fines, with the company filing bankruptcy in 2019.
In what year was Aristotle born?
Aristotle (Ancient Greek: Ἀριστοτέλης, romanized: Aristotélēs; 384–322 BC) was an ancient Greek philosopher and polymath.
In what year did Abraham Maslow die?
Abraham Maslow: Maslow was a psychology professor at Cornell University, Brooklyn College, Brandeis University, The New School for Social Research, and Columbia University.
In what year did Kevin Mitnick die?
Kevin Mitnick: Kevin David Mitnick (August 6, 1963 – July 16, 2023) was an American computer security consultant, author, and convicted hacker.
In what year was Mass–energy equivalence discovered?
Mass–energy equivalence: In physics, mass–energy equivalence is the relationship between mass and energy in a system's rest frame.
Which company manufactures Harrier jump jet?
Harrier jump jet: Hawker Siddeley. The Harrier emerged as the only truly successful V/STOL design of the many attempted during that era.
NHIndustries NH90: Airbus Helicopters. The NHIndustries NH90 is a medium-sized European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter.
Which country is Hawker Hunter from?
Hawker Hunter: United Kingdom. The all-weather/night fighter role was filled by the Gloster Javelin.
Who is credited with discovering Bohrium?
Bohrium: Yuri Oganessian. Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Who is credited with discovering 10 Hygiea?
10 Hygiea: Annibale de Gasparis. 10 Hygiea is a large asteroid in the outer region of the main asteroid belt, between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Who is credited with discovering Nickel?
Nickel: Axel Fredrik Cronstedt. Nickel is a chemical element; it has symbol Ni and atomic number 28.
Home to both edible and poisonous species, this fungal genus supplies the West's most popular cultivated mushrooms, including the everyday button mushroom — which genus is it?
Agaricus is a genus of mushroom-forming fungi containing both edible and poisonous species, with over 400 members worldwide and possibly again as many disputed or newly discovered species.

This central nervous system stimulant treats ADHD and narcolepsy today, but was once prescribed for nasal congestion and depression, and remains tightly controlled due to its abuse potential — name the drug?

Amphetamine is a central nervous system (CNS) stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and narcolepsy; it is also used to treat binge eating disorder in the form of lisdexamfetamine.
Its Latin name means 'water-carrier,' and this zodiac constellation sits between Capricornus and Pisces, in a region of the sky nicknamed 'the Sea' for its watery neighbors — which constellation?

Aquarius (constellation) is an equatorial constellation of the zodiac, between Capricornus and Pisces. Its name is Latin for "water-carrier" or "cup-carrier", and its traditional astrological symbol is (♒︎), a representation of water.
Technically a giant member of the grass family, this plant's tallest species can grow stalks over 150 feet long and weigh up to 450 kilograms — what plant is it?
Bamboo are a diverse group of mostly evergreen perennial flowering plants making up the subfamily Bambusoideae of the grass family Poaceae.

A thin-leaved deciduous hardwood related to alders and hazels, this genus of trees is widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal climates, typically as a short-lived pioneer species — name the tree?
Birch is a thin-leaved deciduous hardwood tree of the genus Betula, in the family Betulaceae, which also includes alders, hazels, and hornbeams.

He won a share of the 1973 Nobel Prize in Physics for an effect he discovered in 1962 while still a Cambridge Ph.D. student — then later turned, controversially, to Transcendental Meditation. Which physicist is he?
Brian Josephson (born 4 January 1940) is a British theoretical physicist and emeritus professor at the University of Cambridge.

This sweet, aromatic orange-fleshed melon goes by different names depending on where you are — 'rockmelon' in Australia and New Zealand, 'spanspek' in Southern Africa — and can weigh up to 5 kilograms. What fruit is this?
Cantaloupe (also spelled cantaloup and cantelope;, or) is a type of true melon (Cucumis melo) with sweet, aromatic, and usually orange flesh.
Sometimes called melde or wild spinach, this weedy annual plant is often distinguished from its relatives in the same genus as the 'white' goosefoot — which plant?
Chenopodium album is a fast-growing annual plant in the flowering plant family Amaranthaceae.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.
This trailing evergreen vine produces a tart berry that starts light green and turns bright red as it ripens on low, creeping stems. What fruit is it?
Cranberry are a group of evergreen dwarf shrubs or trailing vines in the subgenus Oxycoccus of the genus Vaccinium.

This condition's four subtypes include one caused by kidneys that don't respond to a hormone called vasopressin and another linked to excessive fluid intake from a damaged thirst mechanism — what is it?
Diabetes insipidus (DI) is a condition characterized by large amounts of dilute urine and increased thirst.
This social science examines the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services, analyzing everything from individual agents to entire economies. What discipline is this?
Economics is a social science that studies the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
This American physicist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a particle accelerator and later worked on uranium-isotope separation for the Manhattan Project. Who is he?
Ernest Lawrence (August 8, 1901 - August 27, 1958) was an American physicist who received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1939 for his invention of the cyclotron.
With over two hundred species across fifty genera, this bird family includes canaries, siskins, redpolls, grosbeaks, and the Hawaiian honeycreepers — which family of seed-eating passerines?
Finch are small to medium-sized passerine birds in the family Fringillidae.
Found on every continent except Antarctica, this lizard lacks eyelids — instead its eyeballs are covered by a transparent membrane called a brille. What is it?
Gecko are small, mostly carnivorous lizards that have a wide distribution, found on every continent except Antarctica.
Bred for centuries to hunt by sight and speed rather than scent, this ancient dog breed's deep chest, flexible spine, and long legs make it one of the fastest breeds alive. Name the breed?
Greyhound is a breed of dog and a sighthound. It is an ancient breed historically developed for hunting game by sight and speed, and has later been used in organised coursing and greyhound racing.

This field of study concerns the methodological principles of interpretation — especially of biblical, philosophical, and wisdom texts — and has been broadly applied across law, history, and theology — what's it called?

Hermeneutics is the study of the methodological principles of interpretation, especially the interpretation of biblical texts, wisdom literature, and philosophical texts. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
Related to the sodium and calcium compounds found in household bleach, this chlorine-based oxidizer also occurs naturally as part of the human immune system. What is it?
Hypochlorous acid is an inorganic compound with the chemical formula ClOH, also written as HClO, HOCl, or ClHO.
Eaten raw or turned into jams and wine, this round Brazilian fruit is famous for growing directly on the trunk of its own tree — what is it?
Jabuticaba is a round, edible fruit produced by a jaboticaba tree (Plinia cauliflora), also known as Brazilian grapetree.

An Alberta-raised classical liberal who earned his PhD in clinical psychology at McGill and taught at Harvard before the University of Toronto, this commentator drew huge attention in the late 2010s — who is he?
Jordan Peterson (born 12 June 1962) is a Canadian psychologist, author, and media commentator.

Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine and beloved in Singapore and Malaysia, this spicy noodle dish swims in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind, topped with prawns or chicken — what's its name?
Laksa is a spicy noodle dish popular in Southeast Asia.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.

This mammal family, uniting skunks and stink badgers, is defined by highly developed scent glands used to ward off predators, and was only split from the weasel family in the 1990s — what family is it?
Mephitidae is a family of mammals comprising the skunks and stink badgers.
In 1812 Étienne Geoffroy grouped the apes with the Cercopithecidae under the name Catarrhini, or "Old World" members of this familiar simian group — what common name is it?
Monkey is a common name that may refer to most mammals of the infraorder Simiiformes, also known as simians.
This silvery lanthanide, found in the minerals monazite and bastnäsite, is about as common as cobalt or nickel despite its 'rare earth' label — which element?
Neodymium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nd and atomic number 60.
Founder of the charity Volnoe Delo and the industrial group Basic Element, which Russian oligarch led both En+ Group and Rusal until stepping down in 2018?
Oleg Deripaska (born 2 January 1968) is a Russian oligarch and billionaire.
Believed to have originated in Sardinia and cultivated since around the 3rd century BC, this flowering herb native to Greece and North Africa is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.

Named early in the history of microbiology for its widespread presence in water and plant seeds, which genus of gram-negative bacteria includes an opportunistic human pathogen infamous in hospitals as well as plant and soil-dwelling species?
Pseudomonas is a genus of gram-negative bacteria belonging to the family Pseudomonadaceae in the class Gammaproteobacteria.
First flown in 1955 as a nuclear-strike follow-on to the Mach 1 Super Sabre, this fighter-bomber earned the nickname 'Thud' and flew most early Vietnam War strike missions — which aircraft?
Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984.
One of the world's oldest crops, this thistle-like annual plant with globular orange or red flower heads is grown commercially today for oil pressed from its seeds — what is it?
Safflower (Carthamus tinctorius), also false saffron, is a highly branched, herbaceous, thistle-like annual plant in the family Asteraceae.
About 90% of the body's supply of this mood-regulating monoamine is actually made in the gut, where it helps drive intestinal movements — which neurotransmitter is it?
Serotonin (5-HT), is a monoamine neurotransmitter with a wide range of functions in both the central nervous system (CNS) and also peripheral tissues.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.
Discovered independently by two chemists in 1861 via its distinctive green spectral line, this silvery-white metal takes its name from the Greek word for a green shoot or twig — what element is it?
Thallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tl and atomic number 81.
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
This southwestern European viper's bite can be more dangerous than the common adder's — up to 4% of untreated cases are fatal — which species?
Vipera aspis is a viper species found in southwestern Europe.
Passed only from fathers to sons, this genetic structure carries the SRY gene that typically triggers development of male gonads in mammals — what is it?
Y chromosome is one of two sex chromosomes in therian mammals and other organisms.
Genetic in roughly 80% of cases, this long-term skin condition clogs hair follicles with dead skin and sebum, producing blackheads and pimples on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne: Skin condition characterized by pimples.

German-born theoretical physicist celebrated for E=mc² and work on relativity — he won the 1921 Nobel Prize not for those breakthroughs, but for discovering the photoelectric effect. Who revolutionized physics across multiple domains?
Commonly called buffalo, this large grazing mammal endemic to North America is one of just two living species in its genus, alongside a European cousin — what animal is it?
American bison: Species of bovid artiodactyl mammal.

Characterized by extreme food restriction and a fear of gaining weight despite being underweight, this eating disorder is described in the DSM-5 as involving a disturbance in how one perceives their own body shape — what's the condition called?
Anorexia nervosa: Eating disorder. Individuals with anorexia nervosa have a fear of gaining weight, despite the fact that they are typically underweight.
The third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere at nearly 1%, this noble gas takes its name from an Ancient Greek word meaning 'lazy' or 'inactive' — what element is it?
Argon: Chemical element with atomic number 18 (Ar)
From the Greek for "self-devouring," this lysosome-driven process lets a cell tidily break down and recycle its own worn-out parts — what is it?
Autophagy: Process of cells digesting parts of themselves.
Spurred by the 1980 failure of Operation Eagle Claw, this American tiltrotor blends a helicopter's vertical takeoff with a turboprop's long-range cruise — what aircraft is it?
Bell Boeing V-22 Osprey: Military transport tiltrotor.

A French child prodigy who wrote a treatise on conic sections at 16, then built one of the first mechanical calculators and traded letters with Fermat that helped birth probability theory — who was he?
Typically housed in the head near the organs for vision, hearing, and smell, this organ processes thought and cognition while coordinating muscle activity — which organ?
Brain: Organ central to the nervous system.
Native to the Americas from Patagonia to western Canada, members of this succulent plant family thrive in the bone-dry Atacama Desert — what are they?
Cactus: Family of mostly succulent plants, adapted to dry environments.

A German child prodigy turned director of the Göttingen Observatory, this mathematician, astronomer, and physicist made landmark contributions across number theory, algebra, statistics, and probability — who is he?
Carl Friedrich Gauss: German polymath and scholar (1777–1855)
This Italian physician who died in 1909 is considered the founder of modern criminology, arguing that 'born criminals' could be spotted by physical defects — who is he?
Add this steely-grey transition metal (atomic number 24) to steel and you get stainless; polish it and it reflects nearly 70% of visible light without tarnishing. Which element is it?
Chromium: Chemical element with atomic number 24 (Cr)
Found naturally in the sap of the opium poppy, this opiate is a prodrug of morphine often paired with paracetamol to treat mild pain, coughs, and even diarrhea — what is it?
Codeine: Opiate and prodrug of morphine used to treat pain. It usually starts working after half an hour, with maximum effect at two hours.
Caused by a fungus that forms galls on maize plants, this disease produces an edible delicacy in Mexico known as huitlacoche, often stuffed into quesadillas — which condition?
Corn smut: Fungal plant disease on maize and teosinte.
Its Greek name literally means 'boat beard,' describing how its hairy spikelets project from boat-shaped sheaths — better known by a common name evoking a citrus scent, what is this grass genus?
First patented in Germany in 1920 and later synthesized by an American chemist in 1932, this semi-synthetic opioid is roughly ten times more potent than morphine — what is it called?
Desomorphine: Semi-synthetic opioid, morphine analogue. It was first discovered and patented in Germany by a German team working for Knoll in 1920 but was not generally recognized.
Despite its common names, this evergreen conifer isn't a true member of the pine, spruce, or hemlock genera, yet stands as the tallest species in its own family — what is it?
Douglas fir: Species of tree. It is native to western North America and is also known as Douglas-fir, Douglas spruce, Oregon pine, and Columbian pine.

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Found on the forelimbs of most tetrapods, these prehensile, often opposable digits give primates like humans their dexterity for grasping and fine movement — what are they called?

This German chemist won a Nobel Prize for inventing a process that synthesizes ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen gas — a breakthrough that today supports nearly half the world's food production. Who is he?

A Belgian Catholic priest and physicist, he was first to argue that the recession of galaxies proves an expanding universe, and proposed a 'primeval atom' — the first version of the Big Bang theory. Who was he?
Georges Lemaître: Belgian scientist and Catholic priest (1894–1966)
A U.S. Navy rear admiral who helped develop COBOL, this computer science pioneer wrote what's considered the first computer manual and worked on the Harvard Mark I — who is she?
Grace Hopper: U.S. naval officer and computer scientist (1906–1992)

Coined by psychologist Edward Thorndike, this cognitive bias describes how a positive impression in one area, like someone's looks, skews our judgment of them in unrelated areas — what is this bias called?
Halo effect: Tendency for positive impressions to contaminate other evaluations.

Synthesized from the dried latex of the opium poppy, this opioid is used medically in some countries to relieve pain during childbirth or a heart attack — and its 'black tar' form is a crude, variable mix of morphine derivatives — what is it?
Heroin: Opioid analgesic and recreational drug.
The flowers of this shrub genus act as natural pH indicators, turning blue in acidic soil and pink in alkaline soil?
Powered by four underperforming Lyulka turbojets, this aircraft became the first Soviet jet bomber to fly before being cancelled in September 1947 — which plane?
Ilyushin Il-22: 1947 Soviet bomber aircraft prototype. The Ilyushin Il-22, USAF/DOD designation Type 10, was the first Soviet jet-engined bomber to fly.
As president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician spearheaded the creation of the single market and laid the groundwork for the euro — who is he?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?
Soft, dense, and bluish-silver when freshly cut, this heavy metal carries the highest atomic number of any stable element — and its Latin name, plumbum, gives it the symbol Pb. Which element is it?
Lead: Chemical element with atomic number 82 (Pb)
Understood before 1950 purely as the ability to decode written words, this concept later expanded to include the social and cultural dimensions of reading and writing — what skill is it?
Literacy: Ability to read and write.
Encoded by the codons AAA and AAG, this basic, essential amino acid cannot be synthesized by the human body — which one is it?
Lysine: Amino acid. Lysine (symbol Lys or K) is an α-amino acid that is a precursor to many proteins.

The first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the first person to win two, this Polish-born physicist and chemist discovered revolutionary elements and shared groundbreaking research on radioactivity with her husband—making her one of history's most influential scientists. Who was she?
Marie Curie: Polish-French physicist and chemist (1867–1934)
Nicknamed 'meow meow' and chemically related to compounds in the khat plant, this synthetic stimulant produces effects similar to MDMA and was first synthesized in 1929 — which drug?
Mephedrone: Recreational drug. Mephedrone, also known as 4-methylmethcathinone, 4-MMC, or 4-methylephedrone, is a synthetic stimulant drug belonging to the amphetamine and cathinone classes.
Soviet pilots nicknamed this 1972 gunship the 'flying tank,' a helicopter NATO calls 'Hind' that can also haul eight troops and still flies in 52 countries. What is it?
Mil Mi-24: Family of assault and attack helicopters.
Forming dense green mats with leaves just one cell thick, these seedless plants reproduce via spore-topped stalks called sporophytes — which plants?
Moss: Division of typically non-vascular land plants.
The sole surviving family of an ancient cephalopod lineage, these nine living species carry coiled chambered shells 10 to 25 cm across and are all protected under CITES — what creatures are they?
Nautilus: Family of molluscs. It comprises nine living species in two genera, the type of which is the genus Nautilus.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and spread by the fecal-oral route, this is the most common cause of gastroenteritis — what is it?
Norovirus: Type of viruses that cause gastroenteritis.

Numbering 126 species, these are the largest order of marsupials in the Western Hemisphere — and only one of them, the Virginia variety, made it as far north as the United States and Canada. What animal is this?
Nicknamed the 'white rats' of its phylum for how often it's cultivated in classrooms and labs, this single-celled ciliate thrives in stagnant ponds — what is it?
In placental mammals, this is the region of the body between the anus and the genitals, running from the pubic bone to the tailbone, and is often considered an erogenous zone — what is it called?
Perineum: Region of the body between the genitals and anus. The perineum (pl.: perineums or perinea) in placental mammals is the space between the anus and the genitals.
Named after the Latin word for the magpie, a bird known for its opportunistic feeding habits, this eating disorder involves craving non-food objects — what is it?
Pica (disorder): Compulsive eating of non-food items.
Nicknamed the 'terror of Bengal' for choking waterways across the world, this South American aquatic plant is commonly known as water hyacinth — what is its scientific name?
Pontederia crassipes: Aquatic plant native to the Amazon basin.

Marketed under brand names like Sudafed, this nasal decongestant can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant at higher doses, making it both a medicine-cabinet staple and, at times, a drug of abuse. What is it?
